question: Which of the exit ASNs of the 8 run-1 payload lines of ip-proxy/thespeedx-proxy-list are hosting networks and which are access networks? reliability_note says the working exits sat in hosting-provider ASNs rather than residential ones, but the stored lookup (capture sha256:5c310e89dc10b7018e71e9bda779c9d06f1c32c0b8bae69b8903ca1f96b047c9) holds names and prefixes, not network classes, and two of its seven ASNs carry names that suggest access networks: AS17451 BIZNET-AS-AP - BIZNET NETWORKS (the recheck names BIZNET-PREPAID-BLOCK in ID) and AS51004 SCTS-AS Sakhalin Cable Telesystems Ltd.
why: evidence[3] of the record named AS14061 and AS398101 as exit ASNs and called every exit a hosting ASN; this unit dropped that row because the lookup maps no payload exit to AS14061 or AS398101. The same roster, the words all datacenter and the statement that 8 of 8 survivors were hosting ASNs stand in docs/ip-proxy/free/free-lists.md (the section What the survivors are, and the table What kills this class), which lists DigitalOcean AS14061 and GoDaddy AS398101 among the exits of the 8 survivors and omits AS51004 and AS60404; a documents session fixes that prose once the classes are settled from a registry or classification source.
